title: Regularity of purely inseparable base changes of the characteristic-p generic formal fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $n,m\ge0$ and $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] in $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over the formal power series ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; it is a Noetherian domain. Let $K=\kappa((0))=A_{(0)}$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal and $(A_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_rA_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^rA_{\mathfrak p}$ the completion of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].. For every finite purely inseparable extension L/K, L tensor_K ((A_q)^completion tensor_A K) is a regular ring. Noetherianity of the original fibre is not part of this statement.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR, induction and derivation argument

proof.text: Prove the base fibre regular. The power-series ring is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] and a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Mathlib MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing gives regularity of A and hence of A_q. Its completion C is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], hence regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Mathlib Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₁ identifies the zero fibre with a localization of C modulo zero. The proved upstream IsRegularRing.localization instance and quotientBot equivalence give regularity of F. This is implemented by the private helper generic_fiber_regular.

Use strong induction on the finite degree [L:K]. In degree one, Mathlib Module.nonempty_algEquiv_iff_finrank_eq_one gives K ≃_K L. TensorProduct.congr followed by TensorProduct.lid identifies L tensor_K F with F, and transports the base regularity. Finite-dimensional nontrivial field extensions have positive degree, so every other case has degree greater than one.

For degree greater than one, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-degree-p-intermediate] produces M and z with M(z)=L, z^p in M, [L:M]=p, and [M:K]<[L:K]. Install its finite and purely-inseparable instances for M and apply the induction hypothesis to R=M tensor_K F. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-polynomial-degree-p-presentation] to obtain f in R, an absolute derivation D of R with D(f) a unit, and R[Z]/(Z^p-f) ≃ L tensor_K F.

Mathlib Polynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing makes R[Z] regular. Define the coefficientwise derivation using Derivation.mapCoeffs and PolynomialModule.equivPolynomialSelf.compDer. It sends Z to zero and C(f) to C(D(f)); Leibniz_pow therefore computes Dbar(Z^p-C(f))=-C(D(f)). Ring maps and negation preserve units, so its quotient image is a unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular] and transport along the presentation equivalence. This is implemented by the proved private helper regular_binomial_quotient, and closes the induction.

theorem formalFiber_polynomial_geometricComponent
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (n m : ℕ)
    (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))) [q.IsPrime] :
    let A := MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
      (Localization.AtPrime q)
    ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
      [Module.Finite ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
      [IsPurelyInseparable ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'],
      IsRegularRing (TensorProduct ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'
        ((⊥ : Ideal A).Fiber C))
